TERM-ANAPHORA.label: anaphora
TERM-ANAPHORA.definition: Repetition of a word or expression at the beginning of successive phrases, clauses, sentences or verses.
indicators: identical opening words on consecutive lines
TERM-ANAPHORA.distinguishing_test: Is the repetition strictly line-initial (anaphora), a whole stanza repeated with one changed line (incremental repetition), or a broader structural correspondence (parallelism)?

sources.access_note: definition retrieved via search excerpt 2026-11-09; full entry not read

TERM-ANAPHORA.claim_limit: A positional rhetorical label. It says nothing about why the device was used or how a reader responded.

TERM-PARALLELISM.label: parallelism
TERM-PARALLELISM.definition: Correspondence in syntactic or semantic structure between two or more lines or clauses.
TERM-PARALLELISM.distinguishing_test: Does the correspondence cover the whole clause structure, or only the opening word (anaphora)? State which before labelling.

TERM-PARALLELISM.claim_limit: Unverified in this ontology. Usable as a named rival, never as a confirmed classification.

TERM-INCREMENTAL-REPETITION.label: incremental repetition
TERM-INCREMENTAL-REPETITION.definition: Repetition of a stanza or line with a small but meaningful variation, especially in ballad and verse traditions.
indicators: most lines of a stanza repeat verbatim
the changed line alters the situation
TERM-INCREMENTAL-REPETITION.distinguishing_test: Does the changed line advance the situation? If only the opening words repeat, prefer anaphora; if nothing changes, it is plain repetition.

sources.access_note: search excerpt retrieved 2026-11-09; full article not read
definition 'repetition, with variation, of a refrain or other part of a poem, esp. a ballad' retrieved 2026-11-09

TERM-INCREMENTAL-REPETITION.claim_limit: A textual device label. It does not establish narrative progression or a reader effect.

TERM-METAPHOR.label: metaphor
TERM-METAPHOR.definition: A mapping between two conceptual domains expressed in language; the target is understood through the source.
indicators: a concrete image used for an abstract domain
a stated or inferable source-target mapping
TERM-METAPHOR.distinguishing_test: Is there a cross-domain mapping, or only a structural correspondence between clauses? State the reading and its rival.

sources.ref: Lakoff, G. & Johnson, M. (1980), Metaphors We Live By, University of Chicago Press

THEORY-CONCEPTUAL-METAPHOR.label: conceptual metaphor theory
THEORY-CONCEPTUAL-METAPHOR.statement: Metaphor is a cognitive structuring mechanism, not merely a decorative figure of speech.
explains: how concrete images can structure an abstract domain
why metaphors cluster into systematic families
does_not_explain: which mapping a particular reader actually makes
whether an author intended the mapping
